key_insight: Momentum helps RLVR when its coefficient increases as the learning rate decreases, keeping η/(1−β) in a safe regime so expected gains can outweigh sampling fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: Tuning first-moment momentum alongside the learning rate can improve verifiable-reward LLM post-training rather than defaulting to conventional coefficients.
method: Model RLVR as a bandit problem with bias-corrected EMA momentum.
Prove acceleration with exact policy gradients when momentum stays within a no-overshoot range.
Analyze sampled-gradient fluctuations and test predictions in bandit simulations and LLM post-training.
evidence_signal: Bandit simulations validate the predictions; Qwen3-4B-Base experiments support larger momentum coefficients, and increasing AdamW β₁ on Qwen2.5-32B improves mean validation accuracy by nearly 2 percentage points.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on a bandit formulation and a safe momentum range; larger coefficients should not be assumed beneficial without checking stability in practical training.
paper_title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
